In physics, an “impedance mismatch” occurs when two systems each work well but are poorly matched.

In this Science Blog guest post, Harvard physicist Matthew Schwartz argues that something similar is happening with AI and science. LLMs are capable at many things, but working with them as you would with a human collaborator isn’t currently the best way to elicit their scientific strengths.

To address this mismatch, Schwartz created a toolkit for exact calculations in quantitative science. Because similar calculations often emerge in very different areas of science, Claude found connections to ecology, population genetics, and a dozen other fields, and Schwartz worked with domain experts to steer it towards interesting questions.

Read more about these projects here: https://t.co/UpgSwMCz7h

Good morning ☕

𝗛𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘁𝗵-𝘁𝗲𝗰𝗵 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀𝗻'𝘁 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝗮 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺.

𝗜𝘁 𝗵𝗮𝘀 𝗮𝗻 𝗼𝘄𝗻𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺.

Every sleep score.
Every recovery metric.
Every heart-rate reading.
Every pattern in your daily routine.

We generate all of this simply trying to understand ourselves better.

𝗕𝘂𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲'𝘀 𝗮𝗻 𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗳𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗯𝗲𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝘁.

Who actually owns the data?

Most health apps are built on a simple model: collect everything, store it somewhere, find a way to monetize it later.

That model has become so normal most people don't question it anymore.

That's why I find @sleepagotchi interesting.

Instead of building a business around a marketplace for biometric data, Sleepagotchi moved away from that model entirely.

No selling biometric data to researchers.

No giant database of personal health records sitting on centralized servers.

Here's the part that matters:

Your health and sleep stats go to the AI in anonymous form, get processed for the experience, and the data never has to stay attached to your identity.

That distinction matters.

There's a huge difference between:

𝗪𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮.

and

𝗪𝗲 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗼 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝘄𝗵𝗼 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗮𝗿𝗲.

The second model creates a completely different relationship between user and product.

You get the benefits of personalized AI without your most sensitive information automatically becoming another asset on someone else's balance sheet.

𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁'𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝗦𝗹𝗲𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗴𝗼𝘁𝗰𝗵𝗶 𝗴𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴.

The product isn't just telling you to sleep more.

It's exploring how AI can make better sleep easier to understand, easier to follow, more engaging while taking privacy seriously at the same time.

That's a difficult balance to get right.

Sleep data is deeply personal. It can reveal patterns about your lifestyle, routines, habits, even your daily behavior.

So the question shouldn't only be:

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗺𝘂𝗰𝗵 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗔𝗜 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗵𝗲𝗮𝗹𝘁𝗵 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮?

It should also be:

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘁𝗹𝗲 𝗱𝗼𝗲𝘀 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆 𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝘂𝘀?

That's the part of sleepagotchi's approach worth paying attention to.

The company has raised $6.5M. But the bigger story isn't the funding number.

𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗶𝘁𝗲𝗰𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗽𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗼𝘀𝗼𝗽𝗵𝘆 𝗯𝗲𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗱 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆'𝗿𝗲 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴.

A future where personalization doesn't automatically require permanent surveillance.

A future where useful AI can process information without your identity attached to every data point.

And maybe most importantly a future where privacy isn't an afterthought bolted on once the product's already built.

Sometimes innovation isn't about collecting more.

𝗦𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗶𝘁'𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗱𝗶𝗱𝗻'𝘁 𝗻𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗼 𝗯𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗲.

That's a conversation health-tech needs more of.

$CHI @sleepagotchi

Trading history usually tells you what you made or lost.

But it doesn’t always show how you actually trade.

@agenticscredit is taking a different approach with its Agentic Credit Score, or ACS.

score ranges from 300 to 850 and looks at things like risk management, consistency, profitability, trading history and even paper trading performance.

Your score can change as trades close, so your profile keeps evolving with your actual trading activity.

I also like the way Agentics handles the early stage.

If your score is below 580, you can use paper trading to build a track record while the risk engine evaluates your performance. Higher scores can then lead toward the funding pathway and waitlist.

The capital side is non custodial, with funds deployed only through approved venues and predefined risk limits. A qualifying score still does not mean guaranteed funding.

There’s also an Agent Builder for creating strategies through plain language, custom settings or Pine Script.

So you can build something, test it, see how it performs and keep improving your trading profile over time.

$CREDIT system sits around the ecosystem as well, rewarding participation and referrals through non-transferable loyalty points for the planned campaign. They are not tradable and do not guarantee any allocation.

What I find useful here is the idea of turning trading behaviour into something measurable.

Instead of only showing PnL, your consistency and risk discipline can become part of your onchain profile.

Worth checking out if you want to experiment with paper trading and AI-driven strategies.

The October 12 update for @sleepagotchi is starting to feel far more significant than just another reward pool expansion. 

With eleven days left, the real focus is what actually comes after sleep. 

Gotchi Labs has fitness and shopping on the roadmap, but they aren't forcing them out all at once. The rollout for the next vertical entirely depends on where the existing community is already creating real, measurable activity. 

That distinction is everything. Anyone can list five categories and call it an ecosystem. Building one genuinely useful agentic loop first takes actual traction. 

With around 80K daily users already showing up for the live AI Sleep Coach, the focus isn't on how many new verticals they can announce. It is about whether that foundational sleep data is useful enough to power an entirely new product. 

Without that base, adding more specialized agents just creates empty features. 

For now, my attention stays exactly where the utility is: logging my nights, checking the coach, and watching whether my routine actually improves. Still here through the 12th.

records.text:
Anthropic 今天给 Claude Code 推出了 Mod 功能。Claude Code 是 Anthropic 做的 AI 编程助手，你用大白话告诉它要做什么，它自己读代码、改代码、运行命令。

Mod 这个词来自游戏圈，玩家给游戏装 MOD，可以改画面、加道具、换玩法。比如我们以前玩过的《反恐精英》最早就是作为游戏《半条命》（Half-Life）的一个 Mod。

现在 Claude Code 也能这样改了。

Mod 就是一小段程序，用 TypeScript（一种常用的编程语言）写。不会编程也没关系，直接跟 Claude Code 说你想要什么效果，它会自己把 Mod 写好、装上，马上生效，不用重启。

【它是怎么起作用的】

可以把 Claude Code 干活的过程想成一条流水线：接到你的要求，交给 AI 模型思考，模型决定读哪个文件、运行哪条命令，某些步骤要先问你同不同意，最后把结果显示在屏幕上。每到一个环节，Claude Code 都会发出一个信号，表示“我要做这件事了”。Mod 守在这些环节旁边，可以直接放行，可以改一改再放行，也可以拦下来自己处理。

举几个例子。你的要求发给模型之前，Mod 可以自动补一句“请用中文回答”；Claude 要读的文件里有密码，Mod 可以先把密码涂掉；Claude 想运行一条可能删掉数据的命令，Mod 可以拦下来，让你再确认一次。

Mod 还能改屏幕上的样子，比如在对话旁边加一个小窗口，显示团队的代码有没有通过自动测试，或者在输入框上方加几个按钮。

Anthropic 自己也开始用 Mod 搭产品。Claude Code 自带的 /diff 命令（显示改了哪些代码）现在就是一个 Mod，你可以关掉它，或者换成自己写的版本。官方计划把更多自带功能改成 Mod，以后用户可以只留一个精简的核心，其他功能按需加。

安装方式和普通插件一样，在 Claude Code 里输入 /plugin 就能找到。需要 Claude Code 2.1.287 或更新的版本，功能默认打开。

【要小心的地方】

Mod 拥有和 Claude Code 一样的权限，中间没有任何隔离。装上一个 Mod，它就能读写你电脑里的文件，看到你存的 API 密钥（调用 AI 服务用的“账号密码”），看到你发的每一句话，还能不经过你就替你批准操作。所以官方建议只装信得过的人做的 Mod。公司的管理员可以限制员工能装哪些 Mod，Team 和 Enterprise 版还会默认先加载一个安全 Mod，防止其他 Mod 绕过公司定的安全规则。

【和 DeepSeek Harness 比一比】

今年 8 月 13 日，DeepSeek 发布了开源的 DeepSeek Harness，也是一个 AI 智能体工具，能写代码，也能整理文件、分析表格、做幻灯片，GitHub 上已经有 24 万多人收藏。它的口号是“一切皆插件”，连连接 AI 模型的部分、管理工具的部分，甚至负责“想一步、做一步”的核心循环，都是可以拆下来换掉的插件。

两家想做的事一样，都是让用户自己定制 AI 助手，起点不同。

DeepSeek Harness 从一开始就是拼装式的。代码完全公开，用的是 MIT 协议（随便用、随便改），后面接哪家模型也由你选，DeepSeek 的、别家的、自己电脑上跑的都行。它甚至可以把任务转交给 Claude Code 或 OpenAI 的 Codex 去做，再把结果收回来。代价是它还在开发者预览阶段，官方提醒后续更新可能和旧版本不兼容，今天写的插件过一阵可能就用不了。

Claude Code 是闭源产品，绑定 Anthropic 自家的模型。Mod 相当于在一个已经建好的房子上开了很多扇门，能改的地方越来越多，但房子还是 Anthropic 盖的。Anthropic 说要把自带功能逐步改成 Mod、只留一个小核心，这个方向和 DeepSeek Harness 的“一切皆插件”越来越近。

想换模型、从最底层改起，DeepSeek Harness 更自由；已经在用 Claude Code 的人，现在不用换工具也能做不少定制。

我不知道我这个做法将会狠狠推进数学一大步，还是彻底终结数学。

党哥这里隆重推出The Last Math Competition（“最后数学竞赛”），可能将是全人类最后一场、也将是最旷日持久的一场数学竞赛。

https://t.co/WbogrgA0JX

以下是党哥制定的 The Last Math Competition 的规则：

1. 举办方每周会使用 AI Agent 新增 10000 个纯数学领域的猜想，添加到 ./conjectures 文件夹中；

2. 人类和 AI Agent 将共同对现存的所有猜想进行不同维度的打分，预估这些猜想证明或者证伪的难度，评价猜想的重要程度；

3. 人类和 AI Agent 可以共同提交对于每个猜想的完整证明，以 pull request 的形式提交在对应序号的文件夹中（比如 ./solutions/00000000001/my_submission_20260912041426），其中需要同时包含 LaTeX 源代码、PDF 文档和 Lean 4 项目，经过完整 review 后，完成证明或者证伪该猜想的提交将会被 merge 进来；

4. 举办方将会持续维护和更新一个含有所有猜想相关统计数据的表格。表格中的每一行对应一个猜想的所有信息，其中包括猜想的难度预估、重要程度打分、是否 well-defined、目前是否被证明或者证伪、第一次成功解决的时间、成功解决者的姓名和 affiliation 等信息；

5. 根据现存的猜想、对现存猜想的评估、对现存猜想的成功证明或者证伪，举办方将调整使用 AI Agent 生成猜想的策略，来逐步提高未来生成数学猜想的质量，以及可能逐步提高生成猜想的数量。

由于比赛尚在早期，我们必须声明：在早期生成的数学猜想的平均质量比较差，一部分猜想可能定义不充分或者存在错误的条件，或者存在显而易见的错误，甚至可能 "not even wrong"。所以我们将会根据对猜想的统计数据表格，来提升新生成猜想的质量和方法。

党哥的长远目标是：

1. 经过长期的比赛和反馈，我们将尝试逐步提升猜想质量。在长期大量猜想生成的过程中，我们希望能够创造若干重要猜想，通过对这些重要猜想的证明和证伪，来推动数学知识体系的推进；

Good morning 

gstabilizer Day 9 

Today, let’s look at USDZ minting.

For someone new to DeFi, the word mint can sound complicated.

At a basic level, minting means creating USDZ through the mechanism provided by the protocol.

But the more interesting question is

Why would someone want to mint it ?

The answer depends on what utility exists around USDZ.

A stablecoin becomes more useful when users have meaningful reasons to hold, move, trade, or deploy it.

So when thinking about minting, I don’t want to stop at

Can I create USDZ ?

I want to understand

What does minting enable ?

How clear is the process ?

What assets are involved ?

How predictable is the experience ?

What can I do with USDZ afterward ?

That last question is especially important.

Minting shouldn’t be viewed as an isolated button.

It should be understood as one step inside a larger ecosystem journey.

Mint → Hold → Use → Move → Redeem

The more connected that journey becomes, the more meaningful USDZ can become within the broader Stabilizer ecosystem @stabilizefi

OpenAI just fired three safety researchers for sharing confidential information with an outside AI safety organization.

No names. No group. No word on what was shared. The company says only that its investigation found a "pattern of violations" in handling confidential data.

The timing is the uncomfortable part. The New York Times recently reported that OpenAI allegedly ignored employee warnings about risks in testing new models for months, before the Hugging Face incident.

So the people paid to raise the alarm are gone, the alarms they allegedly raised reportedly went unheard, and we don't know what they said or to whom.

These are the models that will write your code, run your accounts and make decisions about your life. The people who tested them for danger are no longer in the room, and the outside watchdogs just learned that talking to them can end a career.

When the safety team leaves through the door marked "violation," who is left to say something is wrong?
